record.tranche_reason: The post uses sparse autoencoders to investigate quantization effects, but does not test whether the underlying network stores sparse features as overlapping directions or establish the proposed superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The post reports SAE training and feature-activity outcomes for full-precision, 8-bit and 4-bit versions of gelu-2l. These concern the behavior of the SAE under quantization, not tests of the claim versions: it does not measure the underlying model's feature geometry, and the model is a toy model rather than an LLM. Findings are recorded under fits_no_version. Cited results and claims from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The post trains SAEs on gelu-2l and its 8-bit and 4-bit quantized versions and reports only SAE training metrics: L1/L2 loss, reconstruction score and share of near-dead features. It never checks whether the SAE recovers interpretable or genuine features, and never measures the model's feature geometry. It uses dictionary learning as a tool, so it tests no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author finds 8-bit similar to full precision and 4-bit degenerate: low loss and high reconstruction while learning almost no features. The skepticism about interpreting SAE features is argued largely from cited work (a Scaling Monosemanticity critique), not from the author's own experiments.
record.recipe_differences: Trains an SAE on a pretrained gelu-2l model and quantized variants to examine SAE training metrics; it does not reproduce the original superposition experiments or measure their feature geometry. The post says it builds on Neel Nanda's SAE repository.
record.method_sensitivity: Quantization level changes the reported SAE behavior: 8-bit is described as close to full precision, while 4-bit shows a degenerate feature-activity pattern.

fits_no_version.finding: On gelu-2l, 4-bit quantization yields low SAE loss and high reconstruction score while more than 80% of features stay below 1e-5. 8-bit tracks full precision closely.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction and loss metrics can look good while the SAE learns few or degenerate features, for example on heavily quantized (noisy) activations. These metrics alone do not show that features were recovered.

fits_no_version.finding: During full-precision SAE training, the count of active features rises in sudden jumps, each with a transient drop in reconstruction score.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE training shows step-like phase transitions in the number of active features.

record.problems: The post gives mostly qualitative descriptions of plotted metrics, with few exact numbers; it reports results for a toy model and does not compare learned feature identities across precision settings. The author says the 4-bit activations are almost noise, making its reconstruction metric misleading.
record.rows_left_out: No separately quantified result was provided in the text for the below-1e-6 feature graph or the feature-frequency plots; the post describes those plots qualitatively.

untested.parts: Whole version: no toy model of superposition, and no feature-geometry or sparsity sweep.
Whether the SAE recovers meaningful sparse features. Only loss and reconstruction metrics are reported, with no interpretability evaluation.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features. Feature identity across precisions is proposed as future work but not done; the interpretation concerns are cited, not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The post describes Anthropic's 1-layer setup but runs its experiments on Neel Nanda's 2-layer, 512-width GELU model trained on C4 and code. All results are described qualitatively from plots, with only two numbers given (20% and more than 80% of features below 1e-5).

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure the underlying toy network's feature directions, overlap, orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transition or regular geometry.
Does not test whether feature importance and limited capacity cause neurons to be dedicated or shared.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
The experiments use a toy model, not LLMs, and do not establish that an SAE recovers the model's actual sparse features.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units. The post raises concerns about interpretation, but does not test these properties.
Does not test whether the represented features are one-dimensional.
